method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the KHA CKD handbook 5th ed (16 of 88 pages). Numbers compared digit by digit.
source_coverage: pages 1-16 of 88. Clinical action plans, staging table, pharmacological thresholds and referral algorithm NOT retrieved.

claims.claim: RACGP Accepted Clinical Resource; endorsed by ANZSN, APNA and RSA
claims.source_text: has been officially recognised as an Accepted Clinical Resource by The Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP) and endorsed by the Australia and New Zealand Society of Nephrology (ANZSN), Primary Healthcare Nurses Association (APNA) and the Renal Society of Australasia (RSA)

claims.claim: Handbook states PBS subsidy requirements may differ from its recommendations
claims.source_text: Please note that requirements for PBS subsidy may differ from recommendations contained in this guide. ... Please note that some recommendations contained in this handbook may differ to current Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) subsidy indications.

claims.claim: CKD defined as eGFR/measured GFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2 present for >=3 months with or without kidney damage, OR evidence of kidney damage >=3 months
claims.source_text: An estimated or measured GFR <60 mL/min/1.73m² that is present for >=3 months with or without evidence of kidney damage. Or Evidence of kidney damage, with or without decreased GFR that is present for >=3 months

claims.claim: Kidney damage evidenced by albuminuria, haematuria after exclusion of urological causes, structural abnormalities, pathological abnormalities
claims.source_text: Albuminuria; Haematuria after exclusion of urological causes; Structural abnormalities (e.g., on kidney imaging tests); Pathological abnormalities (e.g., kidney biopsy)

claims.claim: Up to 90% of kidney function may be lost before symptoms are present
claims.source_text: Up to 90% of kidney function may be lost before symptoms are present

claims.claim: Fewer than 10% of people with CKD are aware they have the condition
claims.source_text: FEWER THAN 10% OF THE PEOPLE WITH CKD ARE AWARE THAT THEY HAVE THIS CONDITION

claims.claim: CKD is twice as common as diabetes; more than 2 million Australians live with CKD
claims.source_text: CKD IS TWICE AS COMMON AS DIABETES ... more than 2 million live with CKD

claims.claim: 1 in 10 Australians and 1 in 5 First Nations Australians aged 18+ are living with signs of CKD
claims.source_text: 1 IN 10 AUSTRALIANS AND 1 IN 5 FIRST NATIONS AUSTRALIANS AGED 18 YEARS AND OVER ARE LIVING WITH SIGNS OF CKD

claims.claim: People with CKD are up to 20 times more likely to die from a heart attack or stroke than to progress to kidney failure
claims.source_text: PEOPLE WITH CKD ARE UP TO 20 TIMES MORE LIKELY TO DIE FROM A HEART ATTACK OR STROKE THAN THEY ARE TO PROGRESS TO KIDNEY FAILURE

claims.claim: Early detection and appropriate management can reduce deterioration by as much as 50%; new treatments can slow progression by up to 15 years
claims.source_text: IF CKD IS DETECTED EARLY AND MANAGED APPROPRIATELY, DETERIORATION IN KIDNEY FUNCTION CAN BE REDUCED BY AS MUCH AS 50% ... NEW TREATMENTS CAN SLOW THE PROGRESSION OF CKD BY UP TO 15 YEARS

claims.claim: 17% of people commence dialysis within 90 days of being referred to a kidney service
claims.source_text: LATE REFERRAL IS COMMON. 17% OF PEOPLE COMMENCE DIALYSIS WITHIN 90 DAYS OF BEING REFERRED TO A KIDNEY SERVICE

claims.claim: Three out of four Australian adults have at least one factor increasing their risk of CKD
claims.source_text: 3 OUT OF 4 AUSTRALIAN ADULTS HAVE AT LEAST ONE FACTOR INCREASING THEIR RISK OF CKD

claims.claim: Risk factors: diabetes, hypertension, established CVD, family history of kidney failure, obesity BMI>=30, current/past smoker or vaper, history of AKI, all aged >=60, First Nations aged >=18
claims.source_text: Diabetes; Hypertension; Established cardiovascular disease; Family history of kidney failure; Obesity (body mass index >=30kg/m2); Current or past smoker/vaper; History of acute kidney injury; All people aged 60 years or older; First Nations Australians aged 18 years or older

claims.claim: Screening frequency: diabetes and hypertension annually; CVD, family history, obesity, smoking every 2 years; AKI yearly for first 3 years then 2-yearly; aged >=60 once off
claims.source_text: Diabetes Annually ... Hypertension Annually ... Established cardiovascular disease Every 2 years ... Family history of kidney failure Every 2 years ... Obesity Every 2 years ... Smoking / vaping Every 2 years ... History of acute kidney injury (AKI) Every year for first 3 years post AKI, then every 2 years ... Aged >=60 years Once off, unless developing other indications

claims.claim: Kidney Health Check is BP, uACR and eGFR; annually for First Nations >=18 and anyone with diabetes or hypertension
claims.source_text: Individuals at increased risk of developing CKD should be offered a Kidney Health Check (BP, uACR, eGFR) every 1-2 years (annually for First Nations Australians aged >=18 years, and anyone with diabetes or hypertension)

claims.claim: First morning void preferred for uACR; consider ambulatory or home BP monitoring in addition to in-clinic
claims.source_text: uACR (first morning void preferred) ... Consider ambulatory blood pressure (ABP) monitoring or home BP monitoring in addition to in-clinic readings

claims.claim: Kidney Health Check recommended after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and after AKI as a COVID-19 complication or long COVID
claims.source_text: a Kidney Health Check is recommended for individuals who have experienced acute kidney injury (AKI) as a complication of COVID-19 infection and for those with long COVID ... recommended for people who have had hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, including pre-eclampsia and pregnancy-induced hypertension

claims.claim: First Nations Australians experience higher burden, earlier onset and faster progression due to ongoing impacts of colonisation
claims.source_text: First Nations Australians experience a higher burden, earlier onset, and faster progression of kidney disease, due to ongoing impacts of colonisation

claims.claim: Blood pressure goal consistently below 130/80 mmHg for all people with CKD
claims.source_text: Maintain blood pressure consistently below 130/80 mmHg for all people with CKD

claims.claim: Albuminuria goal: reduction in uACR of at least 30%
claims.source_text: Albuminuria | A reduction in uACR of at least 30%

claims.claim: Glycaemic goals: BGL 6-8 fasting, 8-10 postprandial; HbA1c <=53 mmol/mol (48-58), <=7% (6.5-7.5), individualised
claims.source_text: Maintain blood glucose levels (BGL): 6-8 mmol/L fasting; 8-10 mmol/L postprandial. HbA1c: <=53 mmol/mol (range 48-58); <=7% (range 6.5-7.5). Individualise according to patients' circumstances

claims.claim: Potassium goal K <=6.0 mmol/L
claims.source_text: Potassium | K <=6.0 mmol/L

claims.claim: No target serum cholesterol recommended; statin +/- ezetimibe in CKD (eGFR>=15) with CVD risk >=10%, and First Nations Australians with CKD and CVD risk >=5%
claims.source_text: No target serum cholesterol level recommended. Use statin (+/-ezetimibe) to reduce risk of CVD events and death in: People with CKD (eGFR>=15mL/min/1.73m2) and CVD risk >=10%; First Nations Australians with CKD and CVD risk >=5%

claims.claim: Salt <5 g per day; BMI <25 (<23 Asian); waist <94 cm men (<90 Asian men), <80 cm women
claims.source_text: Reduce salt intake to <5 g per day ... BMI: <25 kg/m2 (<23 kg/m2 Asian population). Waist circumference <94 cm in men (<90 cm in Asian men) or <80 cm in women

claims.claim: Physical activity 2.5-5 hours moderate intensity weekly, muscle strengthening at least twice weekly, some activity better than none
claims.source_text: Aim for 2.5 - 5 hours of moderate intensity activity across the week, or at a level that accounts for the individual's cardiovascular and physical health. Some activity is better than none. Include muscle strengthening activities as part of daily activity at least twice per week

claims.claim: Alcohol: no more than 10 standard drinks a week and no more than 4 on any one day; no specific safe level recommended in CKD
claims.source_text: Australian guidelines for 'healthy' individuals recommend no more than 10 standard drinks a week and no more than 4 standard drinks on any one day ... There are no specific recommendations about safe levels of alcohol consumption in people with CKD

claims.claim: Recommended vaccinations: influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19, herpes zoster, other NIP
claims.source_text: Recommended vaccinations for people with CKD aged 18 years and over: Influenza; Pneumococcal; COVID-19; Herpes Zoster*; Other vaccinations as recommended by the NIP

claims.claim: New in 5th edition: SGLT-2 inhibitors and non-steroidal MRAs, revised detection algorithm, culturally safe care guidelines, Aus CVD risk calculator application, stepwise albuminuria reduction, new referral algorithm
claims.source_text: including new treatments (e.g. SGLT-2 inhibitors and non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists), new management algorithms, new information on how the updated Aus CVD risk calculator should be applied to CKD ... New recommendations on a stepwise approach to albuminuria reduction in CKD ... New guidelines and algorithm for referral of people with CKD to kidney specialists
